input.prompt: Painted magazine cover illustration in the 1960s American humour-magazine tradition: gouache and watercolour over a lively pen-and-ink drawing, exaggerated caricature proportions, warm saturated colours, visible brush texture and paper grain. Scene: on the roof of an old 1960s Wall Street skyscraper, a swimming pool filled to the brim with shiny gold coins. A very tall diving ladder rises beside it to a long springy diving board high over the pool; the end of the board is EMPTY. At the foot of the ladder stand four caricatured men seen FROM BEHIND, heads tilted back, all looking up at the empty board: from left, a man with a huge mop of dark curly hair in a long rust-red overcoat holding a notebook behind his back; a slim man in a black suit; a broad man in a black leather jacket; a young man in a navy-blue flight suit with a white pilot helmet under his arm. Other rooftops and towers around. The top quarter of the picture is open painted cerulean sky with soft clouds, left clear for a masthead. No flags, no patches. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing.

Redraw the reference character as an affectionate caricature in the 1960s American humour-magazine tradition: confident pen-and-ink line with crosshatching, loose watercolour and gouache wash, oversized head on a smaller body, head and shoulders, three-quarter view, centred, a knowing little smile. Keep his likeness: huge mop of dark curly hair, round wire glasses pushed up and another pair on his nose, long rust-red overcoat over a cream turtleneck, clutching a fat notebook bristling with coloured page tabs. Background: a burnt-orange watercolour wash filling the whole frame edge to edge, uneven pigment blooms and paper grain. No flags, no patches.
